result.description:
Position: Industrial Designer
Type: Full-time
Employer: Image Embroidery
Location: Canning Vale WA 6155
Salary: $147,000 p/a
About the Business:
Image Embroidery is a well-established embroidery and promotional products specialist based in Canning Vale, Perth, Western Australia. The company specialises in high-quality custom logo embroidery, digitising, and the production of corporate, sports, casual apparel, headwear, and promotional items. Known for its commitment to excellence, quick turnaround, and outstanding customer service, Image Embroidery operates in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that values creativity, attention to detail, innovation, and teamwork. The business prides itself on delivering cost-effective, high-quality solutions and building strong client relationships through professional and reliable service.
About the Position:
Image Embroidery is seeking a highly motivated Industrial Designer with a strong embroidery design focus to join our team in Canning Vale. The role involves creating and developing custom designs for embroidery and promotional products, managing design processes from concept to production, and working closely with clients, sales, and production teams to deliver high-quality outcomes within tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment. This position plays a key role in driving innovation and ensuring design excellence that supports the company’s reputation for superior promotional products.
Key Responsibilities:
Concept visualisation and sketching according to client requirements.
Consult effectively with the sales team and clients about design requirements, product designs, and resolve design concerns to meet agreed outcomes.
Investigate appropriate materials and develop production processes to ensure ability to produce cost-effective products and meet client requirements.
Ensure that timelines are aligned with production schedules and implement cost optimisation initiatives.
Ensure concepts are closely aligned to requirements through the production of detailed plot charts, blue-prints, renderings, and sample designs.
Produce technical drawings and accurately test product designs using models, prototypes, specialist computer software, and computer-aided design (CAD) technology.
Collaborate closely with the production team to resolve any product faults or manufacturing concerns relating to the design, production time, or materials issues.
Collaborate with the sales team, as required, to present designs, samples, and final work to customers for review and evaluation.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Appropriate Industrial Design / Product Design and Development qualifications.
Minimum 10 years’ relevant experience.
Advanced proficiency in CAD software, design rendering tools, and digitising software specific to embroidery and textile applications.
Strong creative and technical design skills with a keen eye for detail and ability to translate client briefs into production-ready designs.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with proven ability to consult with clients and collaborate effectively across sales and production teams.
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment while meeting strict deadlines and maintaining high quality standards.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

result.description:
UTS College provides a pathway for students into the University of Technology, Sydney (UTS), one of Australia's leading universities, and it is our vision to actualise potential and enhance lives through the power of learning, our actions and our people. Our purpose is to provide the best available opportunity for students to develop the knowledge, skills & attributes they need to attain their goals through market-leading courses, teaching excellence and an emphasis on the student experience.

About the Role
The Systems Engineer provides technical leadership and capability across project and business-as-usual activities. The role is responsible for designing, implementing, configuring, maintaining and optimising applications, network and server infrastructure that enable UTS College business operations.

The position contributes to the architecture, configuration, testing and deployment of applications and supporting infrastructure across both on premise and cloud-based environments. It plays a key role in resolving complex incidents, improving system reliability and performance, and delivering infrastructure enhancements aligned to business priorities.

Responsibilities
•	Undertakes or supervises complex installations and de-installations of systems or components, including handover
•	Schedules installation work around priorities and resource availability.
•	Monitors and manages incident queues to ensure incidents are handled according to procedures and service levels.
•	Contributes to developing, testing and improving incident management procedures. Uses analytics tools to track trends.
•	Applies technical expertise to maintain and optimise network infrastructure, executing updates and employing automation tools.
•	Uses network management tools to monitor load, performance, and security statistics. Investigates and enables the resolution of   network-related operational and security issues. 
•	Configures tools and/or creates scripts to automate network tasks.
•	Contributes to the planning and implementation of network maintenance, updates, and security enhancements. 
•	Implements agreed network changes and maintenance routines. 
•	Drives the adoption of tools and automated processes for effective operational management and delivery.
•	Oversees the planning, installation, maintenance and acceptance of new and updated infrastructure components and infrastructure-based services. Aligns to service expectations, security requirements and other quality standards.

About You
•	Experience in systems engineering, infrastructure or related technical roles.
•	Strong expertise in server administration, virtualization, cloud platforms (e.g. Azure/AWS), networking and security operations.
•	Relevant degree or industry recognized qualifications (or equivalent experience).
•	Solid understanding and practical application of ITIL service management practices.
•	Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing infrastructure solutions and automation.
•	Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage complex technical issues.
•	Excellent communication skills with the ability to engage technical and non-technical stakeholders.

What UTS College has to Offer[SA1.1]
•	A flexible work environment, including working from home and from our convenient inner-city campus within walking distance to Central Station.
•	Continuous learning and professional development (including ongoing learning & development opportunities, free LinkedIn Learning access and the UTS Library)
•	An easy-to-use Staff Recognition Program
•	Salary range – $75,000 - $95,000

If this sounds like you, we’d like to hear from you!
For more information about UTS College visit utscollege.edu.au

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 







We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.





To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.








Full-time, ongoing Maternity Manager role, leading woman-centred care.












Support a collaborative team with a positive and empowering culture.












Thrive in a supportive, innovative environment with strong career pathways.















About the Role:












Join our team as a Maternity Manager on a full time, ongoing basis to work at Monash Women's Program based at Monash Medical Centre






We are seeking an experienced and passionate Midwife Manager to lead our dedicated team at Monash Medical Centre Hospital. This is an exciting opportunity to provide visible leadership, ensure excellence in clinical outcomes, and guide a team committed to delivering exceptional women centred care. As the Midwife Manager, you will be responsible for the clinical leadership, operational management, and strategic direction of the maternity service, ensuring the wellbeing of women and their babies remains at the heart of all we do. You will lead with compassion, integrity, and a focus on evidence-based practice within our low-risk model of care, while contributing to ongoing quality improvement and workforce development.






This role reports to the Operations Manager Women's - Clayton, and forms part of our broader Women's and Newborn leadership team.
















About Us:






Located in Clayton, Monash Medical Centre is one of Victoria's leading tertiary hospitals and a major referral centre for complex maternity care.






Monash Women's offers:







Specialist tertiary-level birthing and maternity services 


Access to neonatal intensive care and high-risk pregnancy management 


Antenatal, fetal medicine, and multidisciplinary specialist clinics 


A highly collaborative, diverse, and inclusive team culture







Aligned with Monash Health's 2026-2031 strategic plan, Care, Reimagined, you'll contribute to delivering care beyond the hospital, embracing innovation to provide tomorrow's care today, and creating joy in work - all underpinned by our values of being Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In.






Our people are committed to providing safe, high-quality and timely care while fostering innovation, continuous learning, and community-centred service delivery.












About You: 






You are a dynamic and motivated leader with a commitment to women-centred care and excellence in clinical outcomes. With at least five years of post-registration experience in midwifery and recent management experience, you bring both professional expertise and strong people skills to lead, mentor, and inspire your team. 


To ensure your success in this role you will bring the following demonstrated skills, experience and knowledge:







Demonstrated leadership and management experience in midwifery 


A proven record of clinical excellence and commitment to continuous improvement 


Excellent communication, problem-solving, and organisational skills 


A collaborative approach that fosters respect, innovation, and teamwork 


Postgraduate qualifications in management or leadership (desirable)











Your leadership will reflect Monash Health's guiding principles - ensuring safe, high-quality care, exceeding expectations, and fostering a culture of respect, learning, and community connection.








In Return






Joining Monash Health means being part of an organisation that truly values its people. 






You'll enjoy:













A supportive and collaborative team environment 


Professional development and leadership opportunities across Victoria's largest health service 


Access to salary packaging, on-site staff parking, and comprehensive employee benefits 


The opportunity to make a real impact on maternity services within a connected community setting 


A leadership role within a progressive, innovative, and growing women's health program













At Monash Health, we are dedicated to supporting you to thrive professionally and personally, while you lead a service that brings world-class care to families in our community.






For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Madeline Lang, Operations Manager Women's - Clayton on mobile 0428 748 199



Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

St John of God Bunbury Hospital is seeking an experienced and motivated Deputy Combined Facilities Manager to join our team at the South West Health Campus. In this key leadership role, you will support the management and maintenance of the site's assets and infrastructure, ensuring they remain safe, reliable, and fit for purpose.

Working closely with the Combined Facilities Manager, you will help ensure all facilities and essential services meet operational requirements, regulatory standards, and licensing obligations. You will drive best-practice asset management strategies, optimise performance and reliability, and support the delivery of cost-effective facilities services that contribute to exceptional patient care and hospital operations.

The role is offered on a Permanent Full-Time basis, working 76 hours per fortnight.

The Position:

Demonstrate Lead the maintenance and reliability of critical hospital infrastructure and essential services, ensuring assets are safe, compliant, and operational through risk-based preventative maintenance and best-practice asset management.

Coordinate maintenance activities, contractors, and compliance requirements, including job planning, resource management, permit administration, documentation control, CMMS (MEX) management, and the resolution of plant and system breakdowns.

Monitor and optimise critical building services and asset performance, including HVAC, water, air quality, and medical gas systems, through effective use of the BMS and CMMS, KPI reporting, preventative maintenance, and continuous improvement initiatives.

Drive maintenance planning, compliance, and operational excellence by managing asset data, service contracts, shutdowns, training, documentation, audits, and reliability improvement programs to ensure safe, efficient, and compliant hospital operations

Support team leadership and operational planning by facilitating regular team meetings and assisting with budget development, capital works planning, and asset replacement strategies.

Ensure compliance and governance standards are met through adherence to organisational policies, regulatory requirements, licensing obligations, and workplace health, safety, and fire regulations.

The successful candidate will hold a relevant trade qualification and bring proven experience in a similar facilities or engineering role. They will possess extensive knowledge of building codes, Australian Standards, and hospital engineering services, including HVAC, boilers, steam systems, sterilisation processes, and a broad understanding of mechanical, plumbing, refrigeration, electrical, and building services trades. Experience using a Computerised Maintenance Management System (CMMS) and preparing maintenance documentation and reports is essential.

You will be a strong communicator with the ability to build effective stakeholder relationships and reliable professional networks. Demonstrated problem-solving skills, the ability to analyse and resolve complex technical issues, and a commitment to high-quality service delivery are essential.
